source_text:
Tit 1,13b Ἐπειδὴ πολλάκις ἐπαινῶν ἐπιείκειαν ἐκδιδάσκει, εὗρεν δὲ τοὺς Κρῆτας
χρείαν ἔχοντας ὥσπερ κέντρου τῆς ἐπιπλήξεως, διὰ τοῦτο εἶπεν ὅτι ἀποτόμως
ἔλεγχε. Tit 1,15®16 Πάντα μὲν καθαρὰ τοῖς καθαροῖς. ὁ θεὸς πάντα καθαρὰ ἐποίησεν·
εἰ δὲ ἀκάθαρτά ἐστιν, ἡ κατηγορία τοῦ δημιουρ345 γήσαντος ἅπτεται.
thought_title: Why Paul commands sharp rebuke and why all things are pure to the pure
orientation: Oecumenius is explaining Paul's instructions in Titus 1:13b and 1:15-16, first why Paul commands sharp rebuke despite often teaching gentleness, then why all things are pure to the pure.
pass_a_gloss: Since often praising gentleness he teaches it, but he found the Cretans having need as it were of a goad of rebuke, because of this he said that rebuke sharply. All things indeed are pure to the pure. God made all things pure; but if they are impure, the accusation touches the one who made them.

choices.english: as it were of a goad of rebuke
choices.why: κέντρον is a goad or sting used to prod animals; the simile conveys that the Cretans needed the sharp, painful stimulus of rebuke, not gentle teaching.
rejected: as it were of a sting of reproof

choices.why: This is the fixed glossary rendering for the Pauline command; ἀποτόμως means cuttingly or severely, and ἔλεγχε is the imperative of rebuke.

choices.english: All things indeed are pure to the pure
choices.why: The μὲν is adversative or emphatic, marking the first clause of the Pauline lemma; καθαρὰ is the fixed glossary term 'pure.'
rejected: All things are pure to the pure
To the pure all things are pure

choices.english: the accusation touches the one who made them
choices.why: ἅπτεται means 'touches' or 'lays hold of,' conveying that the accusation reaches or attaches to the Creator; δημιουργήσαντος is a substantival aorist participle meaning 'the one who made.'
rejected: the accusation falls on the Creator
the charge attaches to the Maker

pass_b_english: Since Paul often teaches gentleness with praise, but found that the Cretans needed the goad of rebuke, as it were, he said for this reason: “Rebuke sharply” (Titus 1:13). “All things indeed are pure to the pure” (Titus 1:15). God made all things pure; but if they are impure, the accusation touches the one who made them.
notes: The source text has 'δημιουρ345 γήσαντος' with '345' inserted, likely a page or folio number from the manuscript; the word is δημιουργήσαντος.
